title: Draft: All-Hands March 2026 - Product & Customer Update
content:
Goal: short, portable set of talking points + Q&A for the March all-hands. Focus: product updates (Optimize beta, Dedicated capacity improvements), customer wins, metrics, and a clear ask for org (what we need from teams).

Status: rough draft - lots of TODOs and questions. Will iterate with Asha (PM), Evan (engineering), Samira (marketing) this week.

Topline announcement (one sentence):
- We're rolling Redwood Optimize into public beta and expanding Dedicated capacity SLAs - both move us closer to predictable, cost-efficient inference for production customers.

Why this matters (2-3 bullets for CEO to say):
- Customers want predictable cost & latency; Optimize gives automated recommendations (batching, quantization, caching) that cut unit cost without manual tuning.
- Dedicated improvements reduce variability for enterprise workloads - critical for renewals and new mid-market deals.
- Together these features make Redwood a one-stop place to move from prototype to production.

Key metrics to call out (draft numbers - confirm with analytics before final):
- Optimize pilot showed ~22% average token-cost reduction across pilot customers (range 8-48%). TODO: confirm with bizops by 2/24.
- Dedicated SLA improvements: p99 latency improvement from 320ms -> 210ms for our standard 8k model profile in lab tests. NOTE: lab vs production caveat.
- New customer win: AcmePay pilot moved from proof-of-concept to Dedicated commit (~$120k ARR committed). Need CS quote/green light from sales.

Product highlights (short bullets for product lead/CTO):
- Redwood Optimize: public beta. Features: auto-suggest batching profiles, per-route cache hints, model/quantization recommendations, rollout-safe suggestions integrated into Console.
- Dedicated: new autoscale smoothing and burst mode; can reserve burst capacity for peak windows (enterprise feature).
- Private deployment: GA for VPC install in EU region - early adopters onboarding now.

Callouts / caveats (what to avoid overstating):
- Beta = limited telemetry initially; customers on beta get support from solutions engineering.
- Cost numbers are pilot averages; not a guarantee - T&C language to be handled by marketing.

Customer story (short):
- AcmePay - reduced inference spend for fraud detection by ~30% (pilot) while keeping tail-latency SLAs via batching + caching. CS to provide 1-2 sentence quote.

Ask of org (what we want teams to do in next 30 days):
- Eng: double-check rollout playbook for Optimize suggestions - we need a clear rollback for model-quality regressions.
- Solutions/SE: gather 3 buyer-facing case studies for marketing by 3/10.
- CS: prioritize two pilot customers for Optimize to expand coverage.
- Marketing: prepare blog + product page copy for beta launch; target publish window week of 3/16.

Talking points for Q&A (anticipate these):
Q: Is Optimize safe to run in prod?
A: Beta customers will get guidance and a conservative default; suggestions are non-destructive and require explicit opt-in in Console. SE will help with promos for CI/eval.

Q: Will Optimize change model outputs / quality?
A: The suggestions focus on infra-level optimizations (batching, cache, quantization configs) that are quality-aware. We run a regression check on prompt test sets before recommending changes; customers review before applying. Not 100% foolproof - that's why the opt-in + canary rollout exists.

Q: How does this affect pricing?
A: No immediate price increase - Optimize aims to reduce unit cost. For Dedicated, pricing for reserved capacity remains the same; burst capacity is an add-on. Finance needs to approve any public pricing language.

Q: Will this be available for on-prem / private deployments?
A: The control-plane features for recommendations are available in Private (VPC); on-prem installations will need Solutions to enable telemetry/config sync.

Notes to speaker (CEO / CTO):
- Keep it high-level and customer-focus. Use the AcmePay example. Avoid deep infra details - leave those to engineering breakout or follow-up docs.
- Emphasize reliability + predictability (our positioning).

Unresolved items / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm pilot cost reduction numbers with BizOps (assigned: Evan) - deadline 2026-02-24.
- [ ] Get CS quote from AcmePay (assigned: Samira) - deadline 2026-02-25.
- [ ] Finalize marketing publish date with Asha (assigned: Asha) - 2026-02-26.
- [ ] Decide on public pricing language with Finance (owner: Lucas) - 2026-03-03.
- [ ] Upload final slides to /confluence/INF-679 and attach to all-hands invite.

Rough script snippets (for CEO):
- "Today we're excited to bring two major pieces of product work closer to our customers: Redwood Optimize - a toolkit to make models cheaper and easier to run - and improvements to Dedicated capacity that make performance more predictable for enterprise workloads."
- "These changes are practical: they help product teams ship without building complex infra, and they protect your bottom line as usage grows."

Slack threads / references to include in final doc:
- #product-optimize (thread: pilot-results-2)
- #cs-acmepay (ask for quote)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-optimize/pull/214 (feature flag + rollout hooks)

Speaker flow for all-hands (2-3 minutes):
1) One-line headline (CEO) - 20s
2) Quick customer story (CS/Marketing) - 30s
3) Product details + what beta means (PM/Eng) - 60s
4) Ask of org + next steps (CEO) - 20s

Backup slides / appendix ideas:
- Lab vs field performance table (p50/p95/p99 latency pre/post changes)
- Pilot customers & anonymized results (cost delta, latency impact)
- Rollout plan + canary checklist

Tone notes: concise, concrete, avoid big promises. Keep numbers labeled as "pilot" or "lab" when appropriate.

Other quick notes / scratch:
- Might mention Dedicated SLA tier names (Standard vs Enterprise) - confirm legal language.
- Will we tie Optimize to usage-based credits for early customers? brainstorm with growth.

Next steps for this doc: iterate with collaborators, then produce a 1-slide summary + speaker bullet sheet and upload to shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts before 3/5.

Comments (inline):
- Evan: need to add a short tech note about how quantization profiles are validated.
- Asha: prefer a softer "public beta" wording vs "beta" in customer-facing copy.
